# FDG9163

> DO report the number of values written by a Try-Write method via an `out` parameter.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12.3 Writing Values to Buffers with the Try-Write Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9163
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Report the number of values written by the Try-Write method '{0}' through an out parameter

The text has no body; the introduction of section 9.12.3 describes the pattern. FDG9163 reports an externally visible method named Try followed by an uppercase letter that returns bool and has a parameter named destination of type Span<T>, Memory<T>, an array or ArraySegment<T>, when it has no out parameter of an integer type. That includes Try-Write methods that write a fixed number of values, such as the shape of BinaryPrimitives.TryWriteUInt64LittleEndian, which the example of FDG9169 calls; the text asks every Try-Write method for the out parameter. Methods with another name for the output buffer, overrides and interface implementations are not checked, so coverage is partial. CA1021 (FDG5113) does not report the out parameter of a Try method that returns bool (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Span<T> and Memory<T> types need .NET Core 2.1 or later, or the System.Memory package on .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 (see FDG9137). Adding a parameter changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
